name: Game_GetDataManager
summary: One-shot lazy creation of the process-wide game-data context that owns the master tables (monsters, items, text, maps); every 0x63xxxx table lookup takes it as its first argument.
evidence: The 998 call sites resolve to named functions across every subsystem (Actor2D_CreateFromParamB, BattleScene_BuildUnitModel, Anim_ModelLoad_ByName, ...) and all immediately pass the returned pointer to the 0x63xxxx record lookups, so the 'global data manager' role is now supported by named callers, not just by the allocation shape.

name: maybe_Gfx_GetRenderContextB
summary: Lazily creates one 0x37C-byte process-wide context (vtable g_0010AF90) and returns it through out; a second singleton beside the 0x1F8-byte context created by 0x001052C8. Callers are render-object/resource initialisers and UI popup spawners, i.e. code that needs this shared allocation/registration context.
evidence: Named callers Gfx_RegisterRenderObject, Gfx_ResourceList_Attach, Camera_CreateRegularShakeWork and Fs_CacheSet_Initialize all use the returned context as a shared registration/allocation owner, but none reveals which subsystem the 0x37C object really belongs to, so the honest 'second render context' label is kept.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_SteerTowardTarget
summary: Builds a steering target from a shared 0x1C-byte layout node, converts it into a direction relative to the actor position (f_9C/f_A0/f_A4) and calls Actor_SteerMoveDirection; the shared node is created once and cached.
evidence: The old name 'ApplyPositionOffset' described only the subtraction, but every caller is an NPC motion update (Field_NpcAction_RunTowardTargetUpdate, Field_NpcFallAction_Update/LandedUpdate, Anim_ClipSlot_UpdateArcMotion) and the body ends in Actor_SteerMoveDirection, so the function is the shared 'steer the actor toward the target node' helper, not a position-offset applier.

name: maybe_Ui_SceneFlow_UpdateSharedSprite
summary: Ensures the shared 0x98-byte UI sprite helper exists (created once through Ui_Object_InitHeader) and then updates the current selection cursor and the 2D sprite state for this scene-flow step.
evidence: Its only real caller is Ui_SceneFlow_Update (0x0019E45C), and the body does work after the lazy creation (Ui_Part_HasVisibleChild check, Field_Gimmick_UpdateSelectionCursor, Field2D_Sprite_UpdateState), so it is not a plain getter as the old name said: it is the scene-flow's shared-sprite update.

name: maybe_Gfx_InitSharedResourceHelper
signature: void maybe_Gfx_InitSharedResourceHelper(char* once, u32 p1, u32 p2, u32 p3)
summary: One-shot initialiser for a small graphics helper object (vtable g_00299548): after creating it once it issues a layout request and recreates the renderer's resource block through Gfx_Resource_Recreate3C(core->f_14).
evidence: No named callers exist (reached from an init table), and the body is an init sequence rather than the 'reset singleton' the old name claimed, so the name was refined but stays a maybe_.

name: Script_FormatValueForError
signature: void Script_FormatValueForError(void* out, void* value, void* vm)
summary: Fills an sq string for a script error: writes the value's type name from the sq type-name table, or copies the 0x80-byte value payload when the value already belongs to the VM; the object tag is set before and restored after the fill.
evidence: Script_Native_IsZone (0x006F8CA8) calls it exactly on the argument-type-mismatch path before Script_Vm_ThrowError, and the ~230 Script_Bind_* callers are all native wrappers, so 'format the offending value for the error message' is confirmed by a named, high-confidence caller.

name: Ui_Widget_FindPaneAndNotify
signature: void Ui_Widget_FindPaneAndNotify(UiWidget* widget, UiSender* sender, const char* paneName, u32 extra)
summary: Looks a pane up by name in the widget's BFLYT layout and, when it exists, calls the sender's vtable slot +0x20 with the pane plus the widget's +0xd4/+0x10 state; this is the common 'bind my named panes' helper.
evidence: Hundreds of named pane-binding initialisers call it with literal pane names (Casino_Slot_InitPanes passes s_side_lamp_top/s_anim_freespin, Battle_Popup3D_TargetResult_Init passes s_target/s_result), and the same 0x0053D4C4 layout lookup appears in Ui_MessageWindow_BindPanes, so the name now matches named usage.

name: maybe_Gfx_GetSharedCoreNode
summary: Returns the shared sprite/model node stored at core+0xF50; roughly eighty 2D-sprite and model creation paths store the result in node->f_b8->f_128. The decompilation ends in halt_baddata, so the actual field read could not be recovered.
evidence: All named callers are sprite/model factories (Actor2D_CreateEightSpans, Gfx_Sprite2D_InitFromTableA/B, Field_SceneObject_InitSpriteFromLayout), which supports 'shared rendering node', but the body is still truncated and even Gfx_GetContext is not proven to be the only step.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_InitHeader
summary: Initialises an already allocated UI object: installs vtable 0x780384, stores the shared 0x37C screen context at self[1], clears the flag/size words and default-constructs the embedded 8-element array at self+6.
evidence: 124 named constructors call it right after allocation, so it is certainly the object base initialiser; the exact class (Ui_Object base vs. a screen-object base) is still unknown, so the name stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_PartyPanel_CreateSlotObject
summary: Creates the panel's optional 0x30-byte slot sub-object on demand (checked first through the game-work test at +0x24a98), binds it with Ui_SubObject_Ctor and registers it in the panel's notification list at f_4C.
evidence: The only real reference is vtable/table slot 0x72a974 (the similarly named CreateSlotObjectEx is a separate function, not a caller), so the PartyPanel attribution cannot be strengthened; the body still clearly creates a small Ui sub-object and notifies the owner.

name: Effect_FindOrCreateInstance
signature: u32 Effect_FindOrCreateInstance(EffectManager* self, u32 key, int type, u32* params, u8 flag)
summary: Binary-searches the effect manager's keyed tree for a 16-bit effect key and, when the node is enabled, allocates and initialises a 0x98-byte effect instance from the template words, links it into the active list and returns its handle.
evidence: Named callers from field, battle and effect code (Effect_CreateScaledInstance, Battle_ActorAction_SpawnEffects, Battle_TargetMarker_CreateEffectInstance) all pass an effect key and then use the returned handle, matching the keyed-lookup-plus-instance-create shape of the body.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_CreateVariantEffects
summary: Applies the object's variant/effect ids (f_B2, f_B3, the u16 at +0x2CA) by creating the corresponding item model or effect model, spawning the scaled effect for id 0x2B and forwarding to the attached object's effect spawner.
evidence: The body creates models/effects and returns immediately - it does not advance an animation frame as 'UpdateEffectFrame' claimed - so the name was corrected to the variant-effect creation that the f_B2/f_B3 dispatch actually performs.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_HandleResetEvent
summary: Event-0x10 handler body: hides the fixed model slots, releases the stored effect handle f_2FC, respawns the scaled effect f_300 at the object position and resets the animation-slot table f_2C8..f_2E4.
evidence: The only caller is Field_SceneObject_OnEvent, which calls it exactly for event id 0x10 and then forwards the event to children, so 'variant state B' was too vague; the name now states that it is the reset-event body.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_UpdateEffectsC
summary: Slot 15 of the battle member-widget vtable: computes the member's effect transform, creates the scaled effect 0x450, plays the member's effect SE and, when the record has an effect id at +0x92, creates the keyed effect instance and stores the handle at self[0x49E].
evidence: The body matches the other member-widget effect slots (same self[0x49D]/self[0x49E] handles, same Effect_CreateScaledInstance/Effect_FindOrCreateInstance pair) but the class and slot numbering are inferred from the vtable family, so the maybe_ is kept.

name: Field_SceneObject_InitFromLayout
summary: Initialises a field sprite/effect object from a layout record: reads the record id/position, checks the player's defeat flag, builds the sprite actor and effect sprite and computes the final spawn position.
evidence: The body consumes a layout record (u8 at +0x12, u16 at +8, floats at +0x10) and creates the sprite/effect objects; the same layout offsets are used by the scene-object initialisers that call it, supporting 'init from layout'.

name: maybe_Field_Marker_OnShow
summary: Show handler: calls Field_SceneObject_Show and, when the marker still has its effect flag and its activity-mask bit, respawns the marker's ambient effect (id 0x496) at the node position and stores the new handle.
evidence: The body calls Field_SceneObject_Show (0x005E78E4) and then re-creates the effect, which contradicts the old 'OnPause' label; the handler is on the show/resume side, though the exact vtable slot is not resolved.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChild
signature: u32 Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChild(SpriteActor* self, SpriteTemplate* tmpl, SpriteParams* params, int flag)
summary: Allocates one 0x23C-byte sprite child from the parent's template, copies the frame-rect parameters, stores it in the parent's 8-entry child array (self->f_204, count f_224), links it and returns its index (0xFF when full).
evidence: The body explicitly bounds the child array at 8, increments f_224 and returns the index, and all ~70 callers are sprite/actor/effect constructors (Actor2D_CreateEightSpans, Field_SceneObject_CreateSprite, Effect_CreateMeshEmitterFromParams).

name: Field_SceneObject_SpawnByType
signature: void Field_SceneObject_SpawnByType(u8 arg1, u8 arg2, u16 typeId, SceneParams* params, u32 arg5, int arg6, u32 arg7, u32 arg8, u32 arg9)
summary: Data-driven scene-object spawner: switches on the object/actor type id and instantiates the matching field actor, map object, effect emitter, sprite or model part using the shared factory set.
evidence: The body's dispatch over type ids and its fixed callee set (Field_CreateActor, Field_CreateMapObject, Effect_CreateMeshEmitterFromParams, Gfx model part inits) is consistent; it has no direct callers because it is reached from the scene-object factory table, so the name is confirmed only at moderate confidence.

name: Field_SceneObject_SpawnByTypeB
signature: void Field_SceneObject_SpawnByTypeB(Scene* self, SceneParams* params, u32 typeId, void* out)
summary: Second, much larger scene-object spawner with the same factory set; additionally handles the 0x10xx type ids (0x1044, 0x1066, 0x1281, ...) that build composite objects.
evidence: Called from Field_Scene_InitObjectTable (0x0033A140) with the scene descriptor, and its 29 KB body contains the same allocation/factory set as 0x00352DBC plus the extra 0x10xx dispatch constants, confirming it is the second spawner variant.

name: Ui_ListSubObject_BaseCtor
signature: void* Ui_ListSubObject_BaseCtor(void* owner, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5)
summary: Base constructor for list-row sub-objects: chains the list-row base constructor 0x00193D84, installs the derived vtable 0x0038AD20 and stores the owner at +0x28.
evidence: Every Ui_ListSubObject_Create* constructor chains into it and the body only overrides the vtable and owner field, which is the textbook derived-base-constructor pattern; the class name is anchored by those named callers.

name: Ui_Widget_Update
signature: void Ui_Widget_Update(UiWidget* widget, const UiUpdateArgs* args, u32 extra)
summary: Generic per-frame widget update: forwards the tick to the bound controller, handles the pending-sound/transition timer, polls the input flags and dispatches one of the widget's virtual state handlers.
evidence: 224 call sites across Ui_LoadScreen_*, Ui_DiveWindow_*, Ui_CommandWindow_* and the menu code all treat it as the per-frame widget tick, and the body dispatches through vtable slots +0x70/+0x74/+0x78.

name: maybe_Ui_StartIntroModelSequence
summary: Starts a scripted model sequence for a UI screen once both engine view layers are ready: creates the 0x1EB0 model/effect helper with id 0x15, binds the screen model, sets the UI mode word and copies the current view rect.
evidence: The name still rests on the model-binding/UI-mode shape; no named caller was found (the earlier 'Ui_SlotTable' match is a name-substring collision), so the maybe_ is kept.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_PlaySeOnState6
summary: When the attached actor is in the given state it plays SE 6, stores the handle and snapshots a 0x48-byte template into the window unless its state byte at +9 is already 6.
evidence: The body tests the state byte at +9 against 6 and requests SE id 6 through the sound helper; no named caller or vtable sibling fixes the class, so the descriptive name is kept as a maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_JockeyPanel_UpdateCursor
summary: Advances the panel's cursor/hold timer: after the hold threshold it unlocks the entry and plays the unlock sound (event 3), and forces state 9 when the panel timer expires.
evidence: The timing table at system+0x2A264 and the unlock-sound call are clear, but the 'jockey' class attribution is not anchored by a named caller, so the name stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Actor_Action_InitState
summary: Initialises an actor action: detects the special state byte 'x', stores the action-state flag/timer and plays the action's start sound when the actor is not in that special state.
evidence: Reached only through a vtable (no named caller); the body's state flag/timer/sound prologue is consistent with an action initialiser, but the class is not proven.

name: Ui_Window_SetResultAnimation
signature: void Ui_Window_SetResultAnimation(Window* window, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Chooses the window's result/reward animation (0x0B normally, 0x0C when the page state at f_11E4->f_A8 is 4), requests it from the animation table and stores the handle at +0x11DC.
evidence: The two animation ids and the later handle poll (0x00263258 calls 0x0063071C on f_11DC) match the 'set result animation' role; the class name Window is consistent with the surrounding 0x26xxxx window code.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_PlayVoiceSe
signature: void Ui_MessageWindow_PlayVoiceSe(UiMessageWindow* self, int arg2, int b, int ctx)
summary: When the talk window is active, requests SE 0x1C and stores the sound handle plus the two timing words from g_002AFCE8 in the window object.
evidence: It reuses the talk-window-active test (f_4->f_D38) and the sound request helper of the message-window block, and the only named reference is Sound_CommandQueue_Push_2, which is the sound path this function drives.

name: maybe_Ui_SetValueAndPlaySe11
summary: Requests SE 0x0B and copies the two dwords of the global result block at 0x0036A144 into self+8 and self+0xC.
evidence: The body is a two-step 'play sound then copy a global pair'; no named caller or class evidence was found, so the mechanical name is kept as a maybe_.

name: Gfx_RenderState_Setup
signature: void Gfx_RenderState_Setup(GfxRenderState* self, u32 resource, u32 arg3, int mode, int variant)
summary: Builds or releases one render-state object: mode 0 releases the owned handle and rebinds the block at +0x310, mode 1 allocates/initialises the state buffer through the GPU state builder and then binds it.
evidence: The two-mode body calls the GPU state builder 0x006740E8 and the release vtable slot, and the field layout f_338/+0x310 matches the render-state family; no direct caller exists because it is reached through a vtable.

name: Pack_GetManager
summary: Returns the lazily created global pack/resource manager: an array of 0x220-byte manager slots whose first element receives the vtable at creation; every pack load goes through the returned pointer.
evidence: Named callers do exactly pack register/lookup (Pack_HandleTable_Acquire, Gfx_EffectPack_LoadById, Field_LevelVisualData_Load, Ui_Layout_LoadAndBind_Type1), confirming the manager role beyond the allocation shape.

name: Gfx_ResourceList_Attach
summary: Registers a graphics resource in one of the engine's sorted resource lists: builds the three-word key from the current render context, inserts the node, unlinks it from the previous list and marks it busy.
evidence: Named callers are render/resource initialisers (Gfx_ModelResource_Init, Gfx_CharShadowPass_Init, Anim_ModelLoad_ByName) that need their resource tracked, and the body manipulates the list nodes and f_E4 exactly as an attach/relink helper.

name: Gfx_ResourceTrie_Lookup
signature: unsigned Gfx_ResourceTrie_Lookup(const ResourceTrie* trie, const unsigned char* bits, unsigned bitCount)
summary: Walks the resource lookup trie (12-byte nodes, branch indices at +6/+8) using a packed bit array as the key and returns the node's u16 value unless the node's condition string rejects the lookup.
evidence: Named callers are all resource/model lookups (Gfx_ModelResource_FindValueByName, Gfx_ResDesc_GetValueA..D, Script_GetIntTable1..3) and the branch test on the bit array is identical to Model_LookupIdByKey.

name: Ui_Object_DtorBody
summary: Destructor body for the small engine object base: releases the embedded heap block at +0x14 when the object owns it, resets the vtable/id word at +4 and returns self for the deleting-destructor caller.
evidence: Named callers are the object destructor thunks and derived dtors (Field_Actor_DtorBody, Field_SceneObject_DtorSprite, Field_Marker_Dtor, Battle_Unit_Delete), which all use it as the shared base-destructor body; the old verb 'DestroyObject' did not say it is a dtor.

name: Effect_List_DestroyAll
summary: Destroys a tree/map of effect entries: iterates the red-black tree at f_C, frees every 0x10-byte entry body and the tree itself, then releases the still-active effect and clears the active flag.
evidence: The body is a complete teardown (iterator walk, per-node free, tree destroy, active-effect release); the class is inferred from the effect removal call 0x003603F0, so confidence stays moderate.

name: maybe_Ui_StatusWindow_ClearSceneObjects
signature: void maybe_Ui_StatusWindow_ClearSceneObjects(UiStatusWindow* window, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Clears the status window's 0x40-slot scene-object table at +0x53E4 and unregisters the stored model handles; it duplicates the cleanup tail of RebuildSceneObjects.
evidence: No callers were found (it is likely an unused duplicate or vtable entry) and the status-window attribution comes from the identical table layout in 0x00343174, so the maybe_ is kept.

name: Container_MultiList_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a container that owns several intrusive red-black trees/lists: unlinks the four list heads, erases every node of the tree at +0x1C and returns the object.
evidence: The body is the standard intrusive-container teardown (repeated unlink pairs, successor-walk erase) and it is installed as a vtable dtor; the exact container class is unknown, hence the generic name.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_DtorPooledA
summary: Destructor of a pooled engine object: installs the vtable, drains the intrusive child list at +0x20 (each node's virtual dtor), releases the optional child at +0x88, disposes the inline string and returns the slot to the 0x17C64C pool table.
evidence: The pool-table indexing (index & 0x3FF)*8 and the child/string teardown are unambiguous; the owning class is still unknown and the 'A' is only a disambiguator, so it stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_DtorStringOnly
summary: Minimal pooled-object destructor: disposes the inline string at +0x10 when its ownership flag is set and frees the block with 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: The body is the same inline-string disposal idiom as the other pooled dtors, with no vtable store; the class is not identifiable, so only the mechanism can be named.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_DtorPooledB
summary: Pooled-object destructor: installs the vtable, destroys the two child objects at words 0xA/0xB through their virtual dtors, disposes the inline string and clears the 0x1D6DE8 pool slot.
evidence: Pool table g_001D6DE8 and the same string/free idiom as 0x0017C570 confirm the mechanism, but the class and the 'B' distinction are bookkeeping only.

name: maybe_Container_List3_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a container that owns three child pointers and one intrusive list: installs the vtable, destroys the three children, splits both list ends and disposes the nodes plus the inline string.
evidence: The triple child destroy, list-head split and iterator erase are visible; the concrete container type is unknown, so the descriptive name stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_DtorStringDoubleListC
summary: Pooled-object destructor shaped like 0x002598B4: vtable install, inline-string disposal, unlinking of two list-head pairs, then return the block to the allocator.
evidence: Same field layout as the named sibling 0x002598B4 (list pairs at words 2/3 and 5/6, string flag +0xB); still no class evidence, so the maybe_ is kept.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_DtorStringListA
summary: Pooled-object destructor: installs the vtable, unlinks the list at words 0x12/0x13, disposes the inline string and frees the block.
evidence: Mechanism is clear from the list unlink and string-dispose calls; the class and the letter suffix remain unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_DtorStringListB
summary: Byte-identical twin of 0x002E4488 for a second class with the same layout; only the vtable the caller passes differs.
evidence: Identical body to the named sibling 0x002E4488; no additional context distinguishes the class.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_DtorStringListC
summary: Same destructor shape as 0x002E4488 but with a hard-coded vtable g_002E4C6C; called from 0x004FA004.
evidence: The hard-coded vtable and the identical list/string teardown confirm the mechanism; the class is still unidentified.

name: Ui_ListState_RemoveEntry
signature: void Ui_ListState_RemoveEntry(u32 tag, u32 key, int keep, ListState* state)
summary: Removes one entry from a UI list state: resolves the packed key through the hash table at 0x3DB428, then either unlinks/frees the matching node in the f_10/f_14 list or erases it from the sorted f_20/f_24 tree, optionally only marking the owner.
evidence: Both removal paths and the hash-table lookup are explicit in the body, and the keep flag writes the owner's f_31 instead of freeing; the 'Ui_ListState' class name follows the surrounding UI list code.

name: Str_DisposeInline
summary: Disposes an inline std::string-like buffer when its allocated flag at +0x10 is set and returns the same pointer, so it can be used as an in-place destructor expression.
evidence: The guard byte at +0x10 plus the exact 0x0010EC00/0x0010EC14 string deallocation pair identify the libstdc++ string destructor idiom; the name is generic but accurate.

name: maybe_Container_Node_DtorB
summary: Container-node destructor (vtable install, list unlink, red-black-tree erase, reference release); a code-identical copy of 0x0046B5C0 for a second class instantiation.
evidence: Byte-identical to the named sibling 0x0046B5C0 and only reached through a vtable, so the mechanism is certain but the class is not.

name: maybe_Ui_ActorWidget_DtorBase
summary: Non-deleting base destructor of a UI widget that owns a registry node: unlinks the widget from its red-black tree when the link byte at +0x10 is set and returns the object.
evidence: The body is only the RB-node erase plus 'return this', and the class is inferred from the neighbouring 0x4A3780/0x4A37E8 destructor thunks, so the maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Fs_Entry_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a file-cache entry: returns its buffer/index to the owning table (0x707E0C) and erases the entry's red-black-tree node.
evidence: The buffer-release call and tree erase are clear; the 'Fs_Entry' class is inferred from the file-cache release helper and not from a named caller (it is a vtable dtor).

name: Container_Tree_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a small container: erases every node of the tree rooted at self+4 using the successor walk and releases the header reference.
evidence: The successor-walk erase loop is the same one visible in the named Container_MultiList_Dtor, and the function is a pure tree teardown; the generic container name is appropriate.

name: maybe_Container_Node_DtorC
summary: Container-node destructor: installs the vtable, unlinks the two intrusive list node pairs at +8/+0xC and +0x14/+0x18 and releases the payload reference.
evidence: Same shape as 0x0046B5C0 and 0x00591378 with two unlinking pairs; the class is unknown, so it stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Container_Node_DtorD
summary: Third copy of the intrusive container-node destructor: vtable install, doubly linked list unlink, red-black-tree erase and reference release.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x0046B5C0; the caller Container_Node_DtorDelete shows the family is real, but this copy's class is still unknown.

name: maybe_Container_Node_DtorE
summary: Fourth copy of the intrusive container-node destructor, same body as 0x0046B5C0 for another instantiated class.
evidence: Body identical to the named sibling; no class evidence, so the letter suffix and the maybe_ remain.

name: Anim_Instance_ApplyTemplate
signature: void Anim_Instance_ApplyTemplate(int* self, void* params, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Resets an animation instance (vtable slot 0x10) and copies the large default parameter template g_002D150C into it, overriding selected fields from the caller's parameter block.
evidence: The reset-then-copy-template sequence is explicit and named callers are animation/sprite setup paths (Actor2D_CreateWithAnimInstanceA/B, Field_Actor_InitModelFromRecord, Gfx_Sprite_CreateInstance).

name: Ui_AnimShake_Update
summary: Per-frame update of a small shake/jitter animation: compares the current x/y offsets and speed with the target, rolls a random value when the target is -1.0, clamps the speed and pushes the result to the attached flip helper.
evidence: The RNG call and the final push to 0x00540148 are visible, and the named callers are all Ui pane/animation updaters (Ui_AnimSequence_Update, Ui_GaugeWindow_InitPanesC, Battle_HpGaugeWindow_UpdateShake).

name: Field_Scene_UpdateObjectsFromTable
summary: Large per-frame update that walks the scene object table, syncs transforms/models and creates or destroys the corresponding field objects.
evidence: Its single caller is Ui_StatusWindow_RebuildSceneObjects' neighbourhood function 0x00343174, which also builds the table, and the body calls Field_SceneObject_InitFromEntry plus the sorted scene-list insert - the object-table update role is clear.

name: Field_Scene_InitObjectTable
summary: Builds a scene object table from the map descriptor (count at +0xE54, id array at +0xE50), inserts every record into the keyed tree at self+0x4C and hands the table to the object spawner.
evidence: The body reads the scene descriptor via 0x0066AA7C, fills the keyed tree and then calls Field_SceneObject_SpawnByTypeB (0x00353074) with the descriptor, which only makes sense for table initialisation.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_InitFromRecordB
signature: void maybe_Field_SceneObject_InitFromRecordB(FieldScene* scene, u32 record, int* extra)
summary: Second variant of the scene-object record initialiser (different record layout) sharing the same part-creation and slot-insert path.
evidence: The 660-line body is heavily merged and the record layout differs from 0x0033EB5C; only the shared part-creation calls anchor it, so the maybe_ and the 'B' suffix are kept.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_InitFromRecord
summary: Record-driven initialiser for a field scene object: creates the model/anim/effect parts, positions them and links the object into the scene.
evidence: The body is still partly merged/unrecovered (ends in unrecovered code), so although the part-creation sequence fits, the precise initialisation order cannot be verified.

name: maybe_Actor_RequestLinkedModelStates
summary: Walks the actor's linked sub-object chain and requests model state 2 or 3 for each sub-object whose model is loaded but whose state byte is still unset.
evidence: The body only *requests* state 2/3 through 0x003368C8 while traversing the link list; it does not resolve dependencies as the old name implied, so the name was corrected to the actual effect.

name: Field_Scene_ResolveObjectLinks
summary: Resolves the scene's two object-handle lists (+0x1B8 and +0x1A0) to real objects and stores the resolved pointers in the objects' link fields 0x8B/0x98.
evidence: Both handle lists and the two stores are explicit, and the only caller is the scene rebuild routine 0x00343174, matching a post-load link-resolution step.

name: Script_Registry_LinkObject
summary: Registers a script-referenced object in the class registry/hash table and wires the object's back-link at f_C so it can be found from its script handle.
evidence: The body is a single Script_HashTable_GetOrInsert(f_14) followed by result->f_C = self, and named script helpers (Script_Vm_RegisterDefaultDelegates, Script_ToString, Script_VmInit) are the callers.

name: Ui_TextWidget_Ctor
signature: UiTextWidget* Ui_TextWidget_Ctor(UiTextWidget* self, u32 id, u32 arg3)
summary: Constructs a text-widget node: self-links its intrusive list, lazily creates the shared global registry node, registers the widget there and stores the two ids at +0x0C/+0x10.
evidence: The body is a constructor (list self-link, registry insert, id stores) and every caller is a Ui text/message-window setup routine; the class name follows the vtable's 0x782AAC registry family.

name: Ui_TextObject_CreateMessageGlyph
signature: void Ui_TextObject_CreateMessageGlyph(TextObject* self, u32 recordId, u32 styleId)
summary: Allocates and configures the glyph object for one message character: looks up the character record, fills the 0x3B8-byte glyph descriptor (colour, size, layer, font), registers it in the glyph list and binds its animation timing.
evidence: Called from Ui_MessageWindow_SetTextById and the body performs the record lookup, descriptor fill and glyph-list append; the class is anchored by that named caller.

name: Field_Actor_CreateBillboard
summary: Creates the actor's floating billboard/marker (name plate, quest icon or damage text): fills the 0x224-byte descriptor with colour/scale/font fields, allocates it, registers it with the actor and stores the handle at +0x370; also rebuilds the billboard's rotation matrix.
evidence: The 0x3F42B0/0x3F4510 billboard API pair, the 0x224-byte descriptor and the registration at world+0x140 are all visible; the named caller Field_Billboard_CreateDescriptor confirms the family.

name: maybe_Field_CreateActorRuntimeState
summary: Creates and registers the large (~0x298-byte) field state/actor object from a static descriptor, resolves its derived class through the global handle table and returns it with three fields cleared.
evidence: The allocation/registration body is clear but no named caller exists and the object's role ('runtime state') is still a guess from its size and vtable, so the maybe_ is kept.

name: Ui_PanelMessageWindow_BindWidgets
summary: Binds the panel message window's three sub-widgets (+0x120, +0x13C, +0x158) to the panes of the given layout panel, copying each vtable/handle pair through the container link helper.
evidence: Three identical binding blocks read the g_003ACE84 vtable/count pairs, and the sole caller Ui_PanelMessageWindow_LoadPanels (0x001DE2B8) is the window's layout loader.

name: Menu_Slot_ClearEntryListA
summary: Empties the widget list anchored at self+0x1D8, re-initialises the child container at self+0x1C8 from the template at self+0x264, re-broadcasts reset to its children and refreshes the two panes.
evidence: The pop/destroy loop, template re-init and BroadcastToChildren(mode 1) are explicit; the function lives in the 0x72ACE8 menu-slot table, which anchors the 'Menu_Slot' class.

name: Menu_Slot_ClearEntryListB
summary: Sibling of 0x004A10BC for the second list area: copies the template at self+0x264 into self+0x240, truncates that list to one entry, re-binds the sub-object at self+0x230, broadcasts reset (mode 0) to the children and re-attaches the selected model handle.
evidence: Same template/child-broadcast structure as the named sibling 0x004A10BC, differing only in which list area and broadcast mode it resets.

name: Ui_BindUpdateCallback
summary: Registers an update callback: copies the callback triple from owner+0x488 into self+0x258 (vtable 0x72B0A4 = {0x41D3A0, ...}) and stores the owner pointer at self+0x250.
evidence: The body copies exactly the callback triple and sets the owner back-pointer, and the only named caller is Ui_DiveManager_BindContext, a binding routine.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionUi_Update2D
signature: int maybe_Battle_ActionUi_Update2D(BattleActionUi* self, u32 frame, u32 arg3, void* callback)
summary: 2D variant of the battle action-UI state machine: walks the state word at self[0x882] through the 0x1367/0x1399/0x13DA/0x149B-style states, animating party rows, spawning popup entries and updating models until the sequence finishes.
evidence: The 2D/3D split is inferred only from the near-identical 0x003F5528; many halt_baddata blocks remain and no named caller distinguishes the two variants, so the maybe_ is kept.

name: Battle_ActionSequence_ProcessState8
summary: Handles the actor state 8 with action id 0x1D: pushes the message, plays the SE and sets the action slot's animation (slot 8).
evidence: The body scans the eight action records for f_29==8 and f_28==0x1D, then pushes the popup, plays the SE and sets vtable+0xB0(self, actor[0x44], 8), matching the state-8 handler role.

name: maybe_Battle_ScanUnitIntro
summary: Scans all battle groups for units that pass the world query and unit-condition check, feeds each match to the popup/entry hub for the entrance presentation, advances the group/entry cursor and finishes after the last group.
evidence: No named caller exists; the group/entry walk and the popup hub call are visible, but whether it is an intro/entrance sequence or a generic scan is still inferred from the state constants.

name: Battle_Ui_SpawnSmallPopup
signature: void Battle_Ui_SpawnSmallPopup(BattleUi* self, BattleUnit* unit, int kind)
summary: When the unit is idle or has no spare effect slots, spawns a small popup carrying text id 0x56 (kind 0) or 0x57 (kind 1) through the battle popup hub.
evidence: The two literal text ids and the direct hand-off to 0x003FBE4C are visible, and the caller family is the battle UI vtable; the named sibling Battle_Ui_SpawnSmallPopupB exists.

name: FieldParty_UpdateStateMachine
summary: Large state machine that advances a party-group sequence (waiting for menu/field mode flags, spawning member join/leave effects) one state per call and returns whether the sequence finished.
evidence: 22 named callers in the field/menu update chain (FieldParty_Talk_Update, Battle_PartyMember_Update, Text_Window_UpdateMainStateMachine) invoke it as a per-frame step, and the body steps the state word by 0x79/0xB96.

name: Battle_Ui_UpdateFinishedBalloons
summary: Walks the balloon UI's 32 effect entries and, for the finished ones, plays the completion sound (0x1A/0x1B) through the balloon helper depending on the entry state.
evidence: The loop bound 0x20 over entries at self+0x164, the finished check via virtual +0x10 and the two sound ids are explicit; named callers are UI tick paths (Battle_Actor_UpdateDispatch, Battle_PartyMember_Update).

name: FieldParty_AttachMemberSlot
signature: int FieldParty_AttachMemberSlot(PartyGroup* group, int slot, Actor* actor, int keepEffects)
summary: Attaches an actor to a group member slot, clears or re-adds its special attachment category (0x5E/0x5F) and plays the group's join sound when not in menu mode.
evidence: The attach vfunc +0x30(actor,slot,1), the 0x5E/0x5F category tests and the group join sound are explicit, and the function is vtable slot 9 of the party-group table.

name: Battle_Ui_StartBalloonForAll
signature: u32 Battle_Ui_StartBalloonForAll(BattleBalloonUi* self, s16* textId, int slot, u32 argument)
summary: Starts a balloon on every member (or one member when a slot is given) and refreshes the balloon list entry for each of them.
evidence: The slot<0 branch loops over the member count and applies the same per-member balloon call as the single-slot branch, so the 'for all' behaviour is visible in the body.

name: Battle_Ui_StartBalloonForMember
signature: u32 Battle_Ui_StartBalloonForMember(u32 ui, s16* textId, int argument, PartyMember* member, u32 extra)
summary: Starts a balloon/message on a party member, applies the member state and (for the item state 0x74) the item effect, then refreshes the balloon list entry.
evidence: The member vtable +0x2C(text id) call, the 0x74 item-state branch and the balloon-list refresh match the named sibling StartBalloonForSlot's flow.

name: Battle_Ui_StartBalloonForSlot
signature: u32 Battle_Ui_StartBalloonForSlot(BattleBalloonUi* self, s16* textId, u32 slot, u32 argument, int argument2)
summary: Starts a balloon on the member in the given slot: resolves the member, applies the text, updates the balloon list and handles the state-0x79 (item) case.
evidence: The slot-indexed member lookup through vtable+0x48 and the item-state 0x79 branch distinguish it from the member-pointer variant 0x001F5D14.

name: maybe_FieldParty_ApplyMemberEffectSlots
signature: void maybe_FieldParty_ApplyMemberEffectSlots(void* group, void* paramTable, Actor* actor, int playerLane)
summary: Walks 28 per-slot flags of a parameter table and, for each set flag, toggles the matching attachment/effect on the actor through its virtual interface and registers it in one of the 32 group slots.
evidence: Only reachable through a vtable and the flag table/ids are still partly inferred; the sibling 0x001FD2D4 has the same loop shape, which supports the visual-attachment reading but not a precise class name.

name: maybe_Gfx_Effect_GetOwnerEffect
summary: Asks the owner for its effect object (virtual slot +0x24) and activates it through slot +0x28 when present; callers then manipulate the returned effect's f_78/f_7C.
evidence: The two virtual calls and the subsequent f_78/f_7C use are clear, but only two named call sites exist (0x00654EF0, 0x00670954) and neither fixes the class, so the maybe_ stays.

name: Ui_WindowBase_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the shared list/window base: allocates the UI object through Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs vtable g_00325A30, initialises the -1/0 state words and runs the class initialiser at vtable+0x8C.
evidence: The body is a pure base constructor and 24 named window constructors (Ui_SetupEquipWindow, Ui_SwapWindow_SlotTable_Ctor, Ui_BattleWindow_CtorRows3/4) chain into it.

name: Ui_Object_CtorWithPriority
summary: Common window-base constructor fragment: runs Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x0018FF74 and sets the default draw priority at +0x4C to 10.
evidence: Eleven named window constructors (Ui_ShopWindow_Ctor, Ui_PokerWindow_Ctor, Ui_PrizeWindow_Init, Ui_BigWindow_CtorBase) call it, and the only body actions are the base ctor, vtable and priority store.

name: Ui_WidgetCtor_vt21E190
summary: Constructor stub: base-constructs through Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x0021E190 and default-constructs three 0x50-byte children at +0x4C.
evidence: The body is exactly base ctor + vtable + std_ConstructArray(..., 0x50, 3), and named callers Ui_MessageWindow_CtorLayout2, Ui_MultiTextWindow_Ctor and Ui_DiveForm_Ctor are widget constructors.

name: Ui_Row_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the scrolling-list row base: allocates through Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x003B65D4, sets the -1 index sentinel at +0x4A and zeroes the 0x7C-byte inline buffer.
evidence: The -1 sentinel, the zeroed row buffer and the vtable are a row-constructor signature, and named callers Ui_TwoColumnRow_InitPanes, Ui_ShopWindow_CreateSubObjects and Ui_SmithMenu_Ctor build list rows.

name: Ui_MenuWindowCtor_vt22A93C
summary: Constructor stub: base-constructs through Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x0022A93C and default-constructs two 0x24-byte children at +0x4C.
evidence: Body is base ctor + vtable + std_ConstructArray(..., 0x24, 2), and its caller Ui_ItemMenu_CreateRoot confirms the menu-window family.

name: Ui_TimerDisplayPart_Ctor
summary: In-place constructor of a tiny Ui_Object-derived part that owns one animation-reference list at +0x4C; Ui_TimerDisplay_Ctor instantiates it twice inside the countdown display.
evidence: The only external caller is Ui_TimerDisplay_Ctor, which calls it twice on embedded fields f_DC/f_9C, and the vtable 0x765420's slot 0x003680DC binds one animation record - a timer-display part.

name: Ui_TwoTextWindow_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a small window with two animation-reference text elements and one inline intrusive list; installs vtable 0x3D5A64 and returns the base of the enclosing object.
evidence: Two Ui_AnimRefList constructions at +0x50 stride and the vtable install are visible, and the only named caller is Battle_TextWindow_Ctor, which needs exactly a two-text window.

name: Ui_SakusenWindow_Data_Ctor
summary: Constructor for the 22-word data block used by the strategy ('sakusen') window: installs its vtable and zeroes every field from +0x4C to +0xA0.
evidence: It is called by Ui_SakusenWindow_Ctor (0x002A3E78) and Ui_SetupSakusenWindow, and its whole body is the vtable store plus the 22-word clear.

name: Ui_SkillPanel_InitParts
summary: Placement-constructs the four 0x50-byte sub-parts of the skill-panel window inside the caller's object and returns the panel base pointer.
evidence: Four consecutive Ui_AnimRefList constructions at +0x50 stride plus the vtable/0xFF state set are explicit, and the sole caller is Ui_SkillPanelWindow_Ctor.

name: Ui_Object_CtorWithSlotId
summary: Constructor of a small Ui_Object subclass: runs the shared Ui_Object constructor, installs vtable 0x00776CE8 and initialises the 16-bit slot id at +0x4A to 0xFFFF (no slot).
evidence: The body is base ctor + vtable + the 0xFFFF slot store, and the named callers Ui_ShopWindow_CreateSubObjects and Ui_CasinoWindow_Ctor instantiate selectable slot widgets.

name: Ui_PanelCtor_vt1CA2EC
summary: Constructor stub for a large UI panel: installs vtable 0x001CA2EC on the object returned by Ui_Object_CtorBase and default-constructs two 0x348-byte children at +0x4C.
evidence: The recovered body is exactly base ctor + vtable + two 0x348-byte children, and its caller is a composite constructor that chains this with two animation-reference lists.

name: Ui_Widget_CtorBase
summary: Base constructor for the widget family: allocates through Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x003D2558, clears the two state words and constructs the embedded animation-reference list at +0x54.
evidence: The body is the shared base-ctor shape, and its callers are the derived widget constructors (Ui_Widget_CtorDelegating, Ui_Widget_CtorWithSubObject, Ui_Widget_Ctor_53A8/5B9C/7760E8/77D874/CB9C), so 'Ctor' was too generic and was refined to 'CtorBase'.

name: Ui_LoadWindow_CtorBase
summary: Base constructor for the load/save list window: installs vtable 0x75E5CC, constructs six 0x50-byte row sub-objects, zeroes their state and initialises the shared scroll/cursor parameters.
evidence: The vtable 0x75E5CC has the already-named Ui_LoadWindow_InitPanes (0x002A4A68) as slot 7 and 0x002A4F80 sits directly after it, so the class is Ui_LoadWindow; the old name collided with the real Ui_ListWindow_CtorBase at 0x002CF200 (vtable 0x007602E0, 3x 0x330-byte pages), which is a different class.

name: Ui_Widget_CtorWithSubObject
summary: Constructor of a small UI widget class: runs the Ui object constructor, installs vtable 0x75F9C4 and creates the sub-object at +0x4C.
evidence: Base ctor + vtable + one child construction at +0x4C, and the vtable's slots include Ui_Widget_ReleaseSub (0x291220), matching a widget with one sub-object.

name: Ui_Widget_CtorWithTwoPanes
summary: Constructor of a UI widget that owns two child pane objects at +0x50 and +0xA0.
evidence: Base ctor + vtable g_002C1B68 + exactly two Ui_AnimRefList constructions separated by 0x50, returning the base at -0xA0.

name: Ui_PanePair_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a small UI object that owns two child panes: allocates the base UI object, installs vtable g_00319140, creates the two children and resets their animation fields.
evidence: The two child constructions and the 0xFF/0xFFFF/-1 sentinels are visible, and the named caller Ui_TrainingWindow_MemberRow_Ctor uses it as a pane pair inside a member row.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveSubObject_Ctor
summary: Constructor of one of the dive mini-game's small sub-objects: installs the vtable, initialises the sentinel/linked-list fields and creates the child pane used for the dive gauge.
evidence: The class is inferred from the neighbouring Ui_DiveManager_Ctor/0x0032C4BC family rather than from a named caller; the constructor shape itself is clear, so the maybe_ is kept.

name: maybe_Ui_Panel_Init
summary: Constructor of the tiny panel base used by the battle message rows: allocates through 0x001D8B6C, installs its vtable and initialises the embedded text element with Ui_Object_CtorBase.
evidence: Only the caller 0x00293DA4 anchors it and the name 'Panel_Init' is generic; the body shape matches the Ui_Row ctor family, so the exact class remains uncertain.

name: Ui_SmithMenu_SubObject_Ctor
summary: Constructs the small smith-menu sub-object (vtable 0x76E7D4): initialises its state bytes to 0xFF and builds the embedded list at +0x74.
evidence: The call from Ui_SmithMenu_Ctor and the vtable 0x76E7D4 family anchor the class; the body is the vtable install, 12-byte 0xFF fill and sub-list construction.

name: Ui_Window_Ctor_vt7786E8
summary: Constructor of a five-page list window: base-constructs through Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x7786E8, clears the flag byte at +0x49 and default-constructs five 0x70-byte page records at +0x4C.
evidence: The literal vtable 0x7786E8 and five 0x70-byte std_ConstructArray elements are explicit, and the shape matches the sibling Ui_UmaWindow/Ui_ListWindow constructors.

name: Ui_CreateFadeWindow
summary: Constructor for the fade overlay object: allocates the base object, initialises its intro/outro child lists and colour-transform block, installs the fade vtables and stores the caller's screen mode at +0x128.
evidence: The two self-referencing list heads, the colour-transform block and the g_0017BF98/9C fade vtables are visible, and 0x0017BFB4 is its matching destructor.

name: Ui_SlotSub_Ctor
summary: Small constructor used by the slot-machine window family: allocates the UI object through Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs vtable g_00326854 and clears the state word at +0x4C.
evidence: The caller Ui_CursorWindow_Ctor calls it as the generic slot sub-object constructor before installing its own vtable, and the body is exactly base ctor + vtable + one clear.

name: Ui_Widget_Ctor_5B9C
summary: Minimal constructor stub that only installs vtable g_00465BB0 on a freshly allocated Ui_Object.
evidence: The body is exactly Ui_Object_CtorBase + vtable store; no other behaviour exists, so the address-suffixed name is the most honest description.

name: Field_LampGimmick_CtorBase
summary: Small constructor of the lamp-gimmick base object: calls Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x77CF14 and clears the extra field at +0x4C.
evidence: Vtable 0x77CF14 is the base of the 0x77CEFC family that contains Field_LampGimmick_InitModels (0x004FA11C), anchoring the class.

name: Container_HandleResolveAsType
summary: Resolves an engine object handle through the global page table and returns the object whose virtual type query matches this wrapper's registered type id, or null.
evidence: Named callers (Gfx_Sky_SetTextureByName, Battle_UnitModel_SetVariantPaired, Font_ApplyTextToWindow, Script_TriggerEventObject) all use it to turn an embedded handle into the live typed object, and the body checks the page mask 0x000FFFFF plus the virtual type id g_007134FC.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionUi_Update3D
signature: int maybe_Battle_ActionUi_Update3D(BattleActionUi* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, void* arg4)
summary: 3D variant of the battle action-UI state machine: the same states and party handling as 0x003F463C but with the 3D model/camera paths (model creation, attachment update, camera alpha).
evidence: The 2D/3D assignment is still an inference from the structural twin at 0x003F463C; both functions are unreferenced (vtable/table entry) and contain decompiler artefacts, so the maybe_ is kept.

name: Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForModelActors
signature: void Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForModelActors(u32 ctx, int* desc, int fadeMode, u32 arg4)
summary: Spawns an entry that references one or two model actors (name plus number arguments): builds the 0x21C-byte entry, posts the descriptor id (or the default 0x5D/0x24E forms) through the popup hub and stores the two actor ids.
evidence: The entry field layout (+0x208 id, +0x20C/+0x210 and +0x214/+0x218 actor slots) and the name+number message-argument tables are explicit; 48 call sites in the monster-model band make it the shared model-actor entry spawner.

name: Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForWindowRows
signature: void Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForWindowRows(BattleUiWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Populates the action entries for the current window rows: resolves each member row's actor record, calls the per-entry setup, then posts the 0x218-byte pooled entry (id 0x84 / 0x25-0x29 family) and notifies the menu.
evidence: The row loop at self[0xC90] and the pooled 0x218-byte entry with the 0x3FC6xx vtables are explicit; it is the tail block of the battle UI flow.

name: Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnCountBalloon
signature: void Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnCountBalloon(u32 ctx, int* desc, int fadeMode)
summary: Balloon entry for a counted event (e.g. 'N times'): routes the negative count/kind cases to fixed message ids and the positive case to the generic count formatter, then posts the 0x218-byte entry.
evidence: The negative kind constants, the 0xB8A/0xF9D/0xEB5 ids and the Ui_Message_SetNameAndCountArg table are explicit, and Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnCountBalloonEx calls it.

name: Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnEquipCompare
signature: void Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnEquipCompare(u32 ctx, u8* desc, int fadeMode)
summary: Entry used by the equipment comparison messages: carries the two compared stat values and posts the message id at desc+6, with the extra flag forwarded to the popup manager.
evidence: Both callers are the equipment update paths (Battle_Equip_UpdateWeaponSlot, Battle_Equip_UpdateArmourSlot), and the descriptor fields used (desc+4/desc+2 values, desc+6 id) match a comparison message.

name: Text_MessageWindow_Update
signature: int * Text_MessageWindow_Update(TextWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Large per-frame state machine of the message window: dispatches on the window state, advances the current line and drives the balloon/effect helpers until the window reports done.
evidence: The body is the message-window state dispatcher (state ids g_004dd*, line advance, popup clear and the f_D2/f_D3 finish test), and the named siblings Text_MessageWindow_UpdateAnchors/UpdateFragment live in the same family.

name: Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnValue
signature: void Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnValue(u32 ctx, u8* desc, int fadeMode)
summary: Spawns a minimal popup entry carrying a single kind/value pair: builds a 0x20C-byte entry with the kind at +0x208 and the u16 value at +0x20A, then posts it with animation id 0x4C.
evidence: The small entry layout and the fixed 0x4C post id are explicit, and the only caller is Battle_Equip_UpdateArmourSlot, which needs a plain value message.

name: maybe_Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnFlagged
signature: void maybe_Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnFlagged(u32 ctx, int* desc, int fadeMode)
summary: Spawns a flag-carrying entry: builds a 0x214-byte entry from the actor record with the byte flag at +0x211 and posts it with animation id 0x23 or 0xEBD depending on that flag.
evidence: The entry shape and the flag-selected ids are clear, but 'Flagged' only restates the layout and does not identify the message kind; the name stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnUnitEffect
signature: void maybe_Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnUnitEffect(u32 ctx, u16* idList, u32 arg3, u32 fallback)
summary: Populates the display entries for a battle unit effect: scans the id list for the special effect ids (0x173/0x174, 0x13D, 0x289, 0x38D...), builds the matching popup entries and posts them when units enter or leave the battle scene.
evidence: The large id dispatch is visible and the callers are Battle_SpawnUnitEntryEffects and Battle_UpdateActionScene, but the exact 'unit effect' wording is still inferred from those callers rather than from the body.

name: Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnBalloonEntry
signature: void Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnBalloonEntry(u32 ctx, int* src, int fadeMode)
summary: Spawns the balloon/message entry above a battle actor: picks the message id from the sound/message table for the actor, builds a 0x218-byte entry and posts it; the two branches select the left/right variant from the actor flag.
evidence: The message-id lookup (0x0063D7D8), the actor flag branches and the balloon-list update are explicit, and the callers are the balloon/cancel-balloon paths (Ui_Balloon_SpawnForMember, Battle_Ui_SpawnCancelBalloonForMember).

name: maybe_Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForMonsterPair
signature: void maybe_Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForMonsterPair(u32 ctx, u32* desc, int fadeMode)
summary: Spawns a two-monster entry (monster book/encounter message): builds a 0x218-byte entry from both monster records and posts it with the descriptor message id, using the name+number message-argument formatter.
evidence: The two record reads (+0x768/+0x1C), the 0x8B2 id and the monster-model caller (0x00428738) support the monster-pair reading, but the descriptor semantics are not fully proven.

name: Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnMultiActor
signature: void Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnMultiActor(u32 ctx, int* desc, int fadeMode)
summary: Spawns an entry that references up to four actors (four record words, a flag byte and the id): builds the 0x21C-byte entry and posts the descriptor id.
evidence: The body copies desc[0..4] into the +0x208..+0x219 fields of a 0x21C entry and posts the u16 at desc+0x12; the multi-actor layout is explicit.

name: Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnFromDescriptor
signature: void Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnFromDescriptor(u32 ctx, int* desc, u32 animId, u32 actorRec, int fadeMode)
summary: Most general descriptor-based popup spawner: inspects the descriptor id fields (0xFFFF sentinels) and chooses one of the 0x20C/0x214/0x218/0x21C entry forms (single actor, actor+value, multi actor, plain value), then posts it.
evidence: The four allocation sizes and the sentinel checks are explicit, and the only caller is the shared spawn hub 0x003FBE4C used by all action-UI code.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_HandleIdle
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_HandleIdle(BattleSequence* self, u32 arg2, u32 b, u32 c)
summary: One step of the battle action-sequence state machine: when the sequence reaches its idle state (0x1615) it notifies the battle context, clears/applies the finished-sequence effects and returns 1 so the caller knows the step is done.
evidence: The 0x1615 idle-state branch, the context notification and the 0x00640348 battle-mode check are visible; the old name 'Run' overstated it, so it was corrected to the idle handler it actually is, still as a maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForRefList
signature: void maybe_Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForRefList(u32 ctx, u16* refList, int fadeMode)
summary: Spawns a popup/display entry from a small reference list: allocates a 0x218-byte entry, fills it from the referenced actor record (f_768 model id, f_1C variant, f_10 flags) and posts it with animation id 0x0C53 or the mapped message id.
evidence: The 0x218 entry layout and the 0xC53 post id are explicit, but the 'RefList' descriptor interpretation rests on one caller and stays a maybe_.

name: Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForActorPair
signature: void Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForActorPair(u32 ctx, u32* desc, int fadeMode)
summary: Spawns an entry that references two actor records (source and target): builds the 0x21C-byte entry from both records and posts it with the message id stored in the descriptor.
evidence: The two actor slots at +0x20C/+0x210 and +0x214/+0x218 plus the descriptor id at desc+0xC are explicit, and the callers are member-message helpers.

name: Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForStatus
signature: void Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForStatus(u32 ctx, u8* desc, int fadeMode)
summary: Spawns an entry for one actor status change: builds a 0x218-byte entry from the actor record and, depending on the flag byte at desc+0xA, posts it with animation id 0x18 or 0x8BE (the 'state applied/removed' pair).
evidence: The two ids and the descriptor flag branch are explicit, and the caller Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_PushMenuValues is the status-message path.

name: Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnNameCodeBalloon
signature: void Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnNameCodeBalloon(u32 ctx, u8* desc, int fadeMode)
summary: Balloon entry carrying a name/code argument pair: builds a 0x218-byte entry from the actor record and the descriptor u16 code, resolves the message id through the message table and posts it (or the fixed 0x8BE id when flagged).

name: Battle_Ui_UpdateLevelUpPopup

evidence: The three state constants, the unit animation ids and the popup clear/post calls are explicit, and the named sibling Battle_Ui_LevelUpPopup_Dtor exists in the same family.
